title: Mosque of Amr ibn al-As
source: Retained Wikidata reference point, current named viewer building/courtyard and standard PMTiles/DEM plus two inspected photographs.
identityStatus: The retained Q683511 reference point [31.233161111,30.010138888] is unchanged. Its older record was reference-only with no resolved facing or footprint. Current Protomaps building 52776559533054 has 12 raw outer vertices and one four-vertex open courtyard, with a same-ID POI named Amr Ibn Al-As / عمرو بن العاص and nearby matching POI 35184400916520. These current named map controls support the identity and approximate fit; no historical exact way ID is invented. Heading 0.8687951695772824 rad aligns the first mapped courtyard edge with positive X, approximately northeast; positive Z is southeast. Exterior facing sense remains a visualization approximation. The raw outer outline and courtyard are retained exactly. Pavilion center is the mean courtyard vertex position; eight columns, canopy/dome, arcade spacing and two estimated northwest-wall minaret centers [-62,-55] / [39,-56] are architectural reconstruction. Surrounding city buildings, gardens, fence, roads and cemetery remain host content.

reconstruction.heightBasis: No retained or current numeric height or level count exists. Retained width/length statements include 120×120 m and 17×29 m with no common temporal qualifier; preserve them without combining them or forcing the current map to those dimensions. Current mapped outline supplies horizontal scale. Picture-led heights above working floor: paving 1 m; court columns/capitals to 5.2 m, pointed court arches to 8.8 m, spandrels/soffit 9.8–10.3 m, flat roof 10.8 m and selected merlons to 12 m. The octagonal courtyard canopy is about 7.4 m high, pale dome to 13.2 m and finial 14.4 m. Twin minarets are estimated at 30 m overall, with lower shaft to 18 m, projecting balcony around 18–19.3 m, smaller upper stage to 24 m and pale conical cap/finial to 30 m. Detailed dome profile, gallery, exterior openings, tiers, thresholds and all vertical dimensions remain estimates; no surveyed engineering or furnished interior claim.
reconstruction.scope: Individual medium-fi Mosque of Amr ibn al-As: current named outer footprint and exact open court, four roofed pointed arcades with pale columns, low exterior arched-window ranges and sparse entrances, stepped merlons, central octagonal ablution pavilion with pale dome/brown canopy and two slender balcony minarets. No generic stand-in; arcade and roof geometry follows this mapped court. Heights, minaret/pavilion positions, bay counts and fine architectural divisions remain explicit estimates. Five existing shared 256² graphs serve six merged roles and four separate browser LODs. Fine inscriptions, historic carving, tap furniture, fence, garden/city and furnished interiors omitted.
